title: Five-petal flower round
subtitle: A flat five-petal flower motif worked in the round in two colours
excerpt: Five rounded petals radiate from a raised centre worked in a contrast colour, giving a stylised flat flower with a clear stem-and-petal geometry. Each petal is a chain loop filled with dc stitches on the return pass. Three rounds produce a 9 cm motif.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1887), five-petal motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), flower crochet section.
heroPrompt: A five-petal crochet flower motif in blush pink petals with a yellow centre on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Five rounded petals radiating from a compact yellow centre, 9 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished five-petal flower measures 9 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Five-petal flower round
chartDefinition.caption: Centre worked in colour B. Petals worked in colour A. Each petal is a chain loop with dc fill on the return pass.

glossaryTerms.definition: A chain arch anchored at both ends to the same base stitch or adjacent stitches, then filled with double crochet on the return pass to form a rounded petal shape.

content.text: The five-petal flower starts with a compact double crochet centre in one colour, then switches to a second colour to work five
. Each loop is a chain-6 arch slipped back to the centre ring, then filled with 8 dc on the return pass to give a rounded petal.
Use a contrast colour for the centre to make the raised dc rounds stand out. Work the centre in yellow or orange for a classic daisy look; match the petals to the project for applique integration.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 5 g petal colour and 2 g centre colour in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: With colour B: magic ring. 10 dc into ring. Sl st to join. Pull ring closed. (10 dc.)
Join colour A to any dc. *Ch 6. Sl st back into the same dc.* Rep from * at every other dc, so 5 loops total spaced evenly around the centre. (5 ch-6 loops.)
*Work 8 dc into the next ch-6 loop. Sl st into the base dc of the loop.* Rep from * around all 5 loops. Sl st to join at first dc. Fasten off. (40 dc across 5 petals.)
Work the compass rose round for a larger 8-section circular motif with a similar petal structure but geometric rather than floral proportions.
